# Finding ∫ 2x⁵ sin(x) dx

I'll use the **tabular method** (repeated integration by parts) since we have a polynomial times a trigonometric function.

## Setting Up the Table

| Derivatives of 2x⁵ | Sign | Integrals of sin(x) |
|---|---|---|
| 2x⁵ | + | −cos(x) |
| 10x⁴ | − | −sin(x) |
| 40x³ | + | cos(x) |
| 120x² | − | sin(x) |
| 240x | + | −cos(x) |
| 240 | − | −sin(x) |
| 0 | | |

## Combining Terms (diagonal products with alternating signs)

$$\int 2x^5 \sin(x)\,dx = 2x^5(-\cos x) - 10x^4(-\sin x) + 40x^3(\cos x) - 120x^2(\sin x) + 240x(-\cos x) - 240(-\sin x) + C$$

## Simplifying

$$= -2x^5\cos(x) + 10x^4\sin(x) + 40x^3\cos(x) - 120x^2\sin(x) - 240x\cos(x) + 240\sin(x) + C$$

## Verification (differentiate the result)

- cos(x) terms: −10x⁴ + 10x⁴ + 120x² − 120x² − 240 + 240 = **0** ✓
- sin(x) terms: 2x⁵ + 40x³ − 40x³ − 240x + 240x + 240 = **2x⁵** ✓

<answer>-2*x**5*cos(x) + 10*x**4*sin(x) + 40*x**3*cos(x) - 120*x**2*sin(x) - 240*x*cos(x) + 240*sin(x) + C</answer>
